messages:
Sam (Acct Mgmt): Heads up — Mistral Health (acct: MH-7890) hit past due on invoice 2026-04-15 for $48,720. They replied saying a huge test run inflated usage, asking to split payment. Need guidance on whether to offer a staggered settlement.
Maya (Finance): Can you paste their exact ask? 48k is material, we should keep it simple.
Sam (Acct Mgmt): Customer proposes: pay $24k now, remaining $24.7k over 60 days (2 installments), and a 20% credit for 'test-run' tokens. They claim we can see test traffic tagged dev-.* in logs.
Olivia (Customer Success): I saw the spike last week in MH-7890, looks like several jobs from ip 10.4.2.0 tagged staging. I can confirm ~32% of that window was non-prod.
Maya (Finance): If CS confirms ~32% test, a 20% credit is reasonable as a concession, but need commitment terms: card on file, first installment within 5 business days, and signed payment plan doc. Also require we reserve the right to pause Dedicated capacity on missed payment.
Sam (Acct Mgmt): Drafted proposed message to send to customer — can I get a quick OK?
Sam (Acct Mgmt): ```Hi Mistral team — thanks for the note. We reviewed usage and CS found ~32% attributable to non-prod traffic. We can offer a one-time 20% credit to invoice 2026-04-15 and accept a staggered settlement: 50% due within 5 business days, remaining balance split into two equal installments over the following 60 days. Please confirm card on file or provide a payment method and sign the attached payment agreement. Per our terms, Dedicated access may be suspended if payments are missed. If we don’t hear back by 2026-06-02 we will escalate collections and consider service restrictions. — Sam, Redwood```
Maya (Finance): Text looks fine. Add explicit dates for installment due-dates and a clause for late fee (1.5% monthly) if missed. Also route copy to billing@redwood so we have a paper trail.
Raj (Legal): Fine with the terms. Tighten the phrase "service restrictions" -> "temporary suspension of dedicated capacity and API keys". Also add an approval clause for credits: "One-time credit is contingent on confirmed dev/non-prod traffic by CS."
Olivia (Customer Success): I'll attach the csv of identified dev jobs and a small note verifying timestamps. Will ping the customer now to confirm acceptance, but recommend we include a short window for them to sign (5 business days).
Sam (Acct Mgmt): OK I'll send with the edits now and CC billing + legal.
collections-bot: Logged escalation: account MH-7890 | balance $48,720 | proposed credit 20% | payment plan requested | next follow-up 1796005620.
Maya (Finance): Once they accept, finance needs the signed agreement and payment trace before we clear any suspension. If they decline, proceed with formal dunning step 2 and copy legal.
Sam (Acct Mgmt): Sending now. If no reply by 1796005620 (roughly 3 days), let's trigger the next step.
Raj (Legal): Agreed. Keep me posted if they push back on the credit or want longer term — we shouldn't set precedent beyond one-time concessions.
Olivia (Customer Success): Pinged customer in-thread and sent CSV. Waiting on reply. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
